meta.status: SEED - compiled from public extension guidance (RAB, FAO, CABI PlantwisePlus, ILRI). Pending validation by RAB agronomists and replacement/extension with the C4IR national agricultural corpus.
meta.kinyarwanda_status: Draft translations - pending review by native-speaking agronomists.

entries.title_en: Maize: when and how to plant
entries.keywords: maize corn ibigori plant planting spacing seed gutera imbuto intera season A B
entries.summary_en: Plant at the start of reliable rains. Rows 75cm apart, 25cm between plants, 1 seed per hole. Use certified seed.
entries.summary_rw: Tera imvura imaze kugwa neza. Imirongo itandukanywa na cm 75, ibigori cm 25, imbuto 1 mu mwobo. Koresha imbuto zemewe.
entries.detail_en: Plant maize when rains are established (Season A: Sept-Oct, Season B: Feb-Mar). Use certified hybrid or improved seed from an agro-dealer (available through Smart Nkunganire). Spacing: 75cm between rows and 25cm between plants with 1 seed per hole (or 75x50cm with 2 seeds). Plant 3-5cm deep. Weed at 2-3 weeks and again at 5-6 weeks. Gap-fill within 1 week of emergence.
entries.detail_rw: Tera ibigori imvura imaze kugwa neza (Igihembwe A: Nzeri-Ukwakira, Igihembwe B: Gashyantare-Werurwe). Koresha imbuto z'indobanure zemewe ziboneka ku bacuruzi b'inyongeramusaruro (binyuze muri Nkunganire). Intera: cm 75 hagati y'imirongo na cm 25 hagati y'ibigori, imbuto 1 mu mwobo (cyangwa cm 75x50 imbuto 2). Ubujyakuzimu cm 3-5. Bagara nyuma y'ibyumweru 2-3 n'ibyumweru 5-6.

entries.keywords: maize ibigori fertiliser fertilizer DAP urea NPK manure ifumbire mvaruganda imborera top dress
entries.summary_en: At planting: manure + DAP about 1kg per are (100m2). At 4-6 weeks: Urea about 0.5-1kg per are, placed beside plants.
entries.summary_rw: Mu gutera: ifumbire y'imborera + DAP ~kg 1 kuri ari (m2 100). Nyuma y'ibyumweru 4-6: Ure ~kg 0.5-1 kuri ari, iruhande rw'igihingwa.
entries.detail_en: Apply well-decomposed manure or compost (about 100kg per are, i.e. 10 t/ha) before planting. At planting, place DAP in the planting hole, about 1kg per are (100kg/ha), covered with soil so it does not touch the seed. Top-dress with Urea at about 0.5-1kg per are (50-100kg/ha) at 4-6 weeks when soil is moist, 5cm from the plant, then cover. On acidic soils, liming improves fertiliser response. Confirm rates with your sector agronomist or a soil test.
entries.detail_rw: Shyira ifumbire y'imborera iboze neza (~kg 100 kuri ari, ni ukuvuga toni 10/ha) mbere yo gutera. Mu gutera, shyira DAP mu mwobo, ~kg 1 kuri ari (kg 100/ha), uyipfuke ntikore ku mbuto. Nyuma y'ibyumweru 4-6, ubutaka butose, shyira Ure ~kg 0.5-1 kuri ari (kg 50-100/ha) cm 5 uvuye ku gihingwa, uyipfuke. Ku butaka busharira, ishwagara yongera umusaruro. Baza agronome w'umurenge cyangwa usuzumishe ubutaka.

entries.keywords: fall armyworm faw nkongwa idasanzwe caterpillar worm maize ibigori leaves holes whorl frass inyo ibinyabwoya amababi
entries.summary_en: Check fields weekly. Ragged holes and sawdust-like droppings in the funnel mean armyworm. Crush eggs/larvae early; use only RAB-approved pesticide.
entries.summary_rw: Genzura umurima buri cyumweru. Imyobo mu mababi n'umwanda umeze nk'ifu mu mutima w'igihingwa ni nkongwa. Yica amagi n'inyo hakiri kare; koresha imiti yemejwe na RAB gusa.
entries.detail_en: Signs: small 'windowpane' patches on young leaves, ragged holes, and sawdust-like droppings in the whorl. Scout 10 plants in 5 spots weekly from emergence. If fewer than 2 in 10 plants are damaged: hand-pick egg masses and caterpillars, and put a pinch of dry soil or ash in the whorl. If 2 or more in 10 are damaged in young maize: spray an RAB-approved product into the whorl in the early morning or evening, wearing protective gear. Plant early and at the same time as neighbours; intercrop with beans or desmodium (push-pull). Report big outbreaks to your sector agronomist.
entries.detail_rw: Ibimenyetso: amababi mato afite uduce tumeze nk'idirishya, imyobo, n'umwanda umeze nk'ifu mu mutima w'igihingwa. Genzura ibigori 10 ahantu 5 buri cyumweru. Niba ibyangiritse biri munsi ya 2 kuri 10: tora amagi n'inyo n'intoki, ushyire agataka cyangwa ivu mu mutima w'igihingwa. Niba ari 2 cyangwa birenga kuri 10: tera umuti wemejwe na RAB mu mutima w'igihingwa mu gitondo cyangwa nimugoroba, wambaye ibikoresho byo kwirinda. Tera kare kandi icyarimwe n'abaturanyi. Menyesha agronome w'umurenge niba ari nyinshi.
entries.source: FAO Fall Armyworm field guide; CABI PlantwisePlus; RAB

entries.keywords: maize ibigori harvest storage stored store mould mouldy rotten drying aflatoxin hermetic bag moisture gusarura guhunika kumisha uruhumbu umufuka
entries.summary_en: Harvest when husks are dry. Dry grain on tarpaulin to 13% moisture (bites hard, rattles). Store in hermetic bags off the floor.
entries.summary_rw: Sarura amashaza yumye. Anika ibinyampeke kuri shitingi kugeza byumye neza (13%). Hunika mu mifuka ifunze neza itageramo umwuka, itari hasi.
entries.detail_en: Harvest when husks turn brown and grain is hard with a black layer at the tip. Never dry maize on bare ground: use tarpaulins or raised racks. Dry to 13% moisture (grain cracks when bitten, rattles in the hand). Remove rotten or mouldy cobs: mould can contain aflatoxin which is dangerous to people and animals. Store in hermetic (airtight) bags on pallets, in a clean, dry store. Do not mix with old grain.
entries.detail_rw: Sarura amashaza yahindutse ikigina kandi impeke zikomeye. Ntukanike ibigori ku butaka: koresha shitingi cyangwa urutara. Kumisha kugeza ku bushuhe bwa 13% (impeke ziravunika iyo uziriye). Kuramo ibigori byaboze cyangwa bifite uruhumbu: rushobora kugira uburozi (aflatoxine) bwangiza abantu n'amatungo. Hunika mu mifuka ifunze neza (hermetic) iri ku mbaho, mu bubiko busukuye kandi bwumye.

entries.keywords: beans ibishyimbo bush climbing stakes spacing planting ibyuririzi imiteja gutera intera
entries.summary_en: Bush beans: rows 40cm, 10cm between seeds. Climbing beans: 50x25cm with stakes about 2m tall. Use certified or iron-rich (biofortified) varieties.
entries.summary_rw: Ibishyimbo bigufi: imirongo cm 40, imbuto cm 10. Ibyuririzi: cm 50x25 n'imiteja ya m 2. Koresha imbuto zemewe cyangwa izikungahaye ku butare.
entries.detail_en: Plant beans at the start of the rains in well-drained soil. Bush beans: 40cm between rows and 10cm between seeds, 2-3cm deep. Climbing beans give 2-3 times more yield: plant at 50cm x 25cm, 2 seeds per hole, and install stakes about 2m tall within 2 weeks. Use certified seed; iron-biofortified varieties released by RAB improve family nutrition. Rotate with cereals to reduce root rot.
entries.detail_rw: Tera ibishyimbo imvura itangiye, mu butaka butareka amazi. Ibishyimbo bigufi: cm 40 hagati y'imirongo na cm 10 hagati y'imbuto, ubujyakuzimu cm 2-3. Ibyuririzi bitanga umusaruro ukubye 2-3: tera kuri cm 50 x 25, imbuto 2 mu mwobo, ushinge imiteja ya m 2 mu byumweru 2. Koresha imbuto zemewe; ibishyimbo bikungahaye ku butare bya RAB byongera imirire myiza. Simburanya n'ibinyampeke.

entries.keywords: beans ibishyimbo fertiliser fertilizer DAP NPK manure ifumbire
entries.summary_en: Use manure/compost plus a small dose of DAP or NPK 17-17-17 (about 1kg per are) at planting. Beans fix their own nitrogen: avoid heavy urea.
entries.summary_rw: Koresha imborera + DAP cyangwa NPK 17-17-17 nke (~kg 1 kuri ari) mu gutera. Ibishyimbo byikorera azote: ntukoreshe ure nyinshi.
entries.detail_en: Apply compost or manure before planting. At planting, a small dose of DAP or NPK 17-17-17 (about 1kg per are, 100kg/ha) in the furrow helps root growth. Beans fix nitrogen from the air with their root nodules, so heavy urea is not needed. On acidic soils, lime (ishwagara) applied before planting strongly improves bean yields.
entries.detail_rw: Shyira ifumbire y'imborera mbere yo gutera. Mu gutera, DAP cyangwa NPK 17-17-17 nke (~kg 1 kuri ari, kg 100/ha) mu murongo ifasha imizi. Ibishyimbo byikorera azote ivuye mu kirere, bityo ntibikenera ure nyinshi. Ku butaka busharira, ishwagara ishyizwe mbere yo gutera yongera cyane umusaruro w'ibishyimbo.

entries.title_en: Bean root rot and bean fly
entries.keywords: beans ibishyimbo root rot wilting yellow bean fly stem rot kuma kubora imizi isazi umuhondo
entries.summary_en: Yellowing and wilting with rotten roots is root rot. Use resistant varieties, drained soil, rotation and manure. Do not replant beans in the same plot every season.
entries.summary_rw: Ibishyimbo bihinduka umuhondo bikuma, imizi yaboze, ni indwara yo kubora kw'imizi. Koresha imbuto zihanganira indwara, ubutaka butareka amazi, n'isimburanya.
entries.detail_en: Root rot: plants yellow, wilt and die; roots and lower stem are brown and rotten. It is worse in waterlogged, poor soils and where beans are planted every season. Control: resistant (often climbing) varieties, raised beds or drainage, crop rotation with maize or sorghum, and plenty of manure. Bean fly: young plants wilt with swollen, cracked stem base; plant early, earth up soil around stems, and use treated seed where approved.
entries.detail_rw: Kubora kw'imizi: ibishyimbo bihinduka umuhondo, birazinga bikuma; imizi n'igice cyo hasi cy'uruti biraboze. Biba bibi iyo ubutaka bureka amazi kandi ibishyimbo bitewe buri gihembwe. Kurwanya: imbuto zihanganira indwara (akenshi ibyuririzi), amaterasi cyangwa imiyoboro y'amazi, gusimburanya n'ibigori cyangwa amasaka, n'imborera nyinshi. Isazi y'ibishyimbo: tera kare kandi wegeranye itaka ku ruti.

entries.keywords: beans ibishyimbo harvest storage stored store weevils drying gusarura guhunika imungu kumisha
entries.summary_en: Harvest when most pods are dry. Dry on tarpaulin, thresh gently, store in hermetic bags to stop weevils.
entries.summary_rw: Sarura imiteja myinshi yumye. Anika kuri shitingi, uhure buhoro, uhunike mu mifuka ifunze neza kugira ngo imungu zitabyangiza.
entries.detail_en: Harvest when most pods are dry and yellow-brown. Dry on tarpaulins (not bare soil) and thresh gently to avoid cracking seeds. Grain is dry when it cracks between the teeth. Store in hermetic bags on raised pallets; this kills bruchid weevils without chemicals. Keep seed for planting separately and label it.
entries.detail_rw: Sarura iyo imiteja myinshi yumye ifite ibara ry'ikigina. Anika kuri shitingi (si ku butaka), uhure buhoro kugira ngo impeke zitavunika. Impeke zumye iyo zivunika uzirumye. Hunika mu mifuka ifunze neza (hermetic) iri ku mbaho; bica imungu nta miti. Bika imbuto zo gutera ukwazo kandi uzandikeho.

entries.keywords: potato irish potato ibirayi planting seed spacing hilling gutera imbuto intera kurunda
entries.summary_en: Use certified seed potato. Rows 70-80cm, 30cm between tubers, 10cm deep. Hill soil around stems twice.
entries.summary_rw: Koresha imbuto z'ibirayi zemewe. Imirongo cm 70-80, ibirayi cm 30, ubujyakuzimu cm 10. Rundaho itaka kabiri.
entries.detail_en: Use certified seed potato from a registered multiplier: farm-saved seed spreads bacterial wilt and viruses. Use sprouted tubers of 35-55mm. Plant 70-80cm between rows and 30cm between tubers, about 10cm deep. Hill (earth up) at about 3 and 6 weeks to protect tubers from light and pests. Rotate: do not plant potato, tomato or eggplant in the same plot for at least 2 seasons.
entries.detail_rw: Koresha imbuto z'ibirayi zemewe ziva ku batubuzi banditswe: imbuto zisigaye mu murima zikwirakwiza indwara. Koresha ibirayi bimeze bya mm 35-55. Tera cm 70-80 hagati y'imirongo na cm 30 hagati y'ibirayi, ubujyakuzimu cm 10. Rundaho itaka nyuma y'ibyumweru 3 na 6. Simburanya: ntutere ibirayi, inyanya cyangwa intoryi mu murima umwe nibura ibihembwe 2.

entries.keywords: potato ibirayi fertiliser fertilizer NPK 17-17-17 manure ifumbire
entries.summary_en: Manure/compost plus NPK 17-17-17 about 3kg per are (300kg/ha) in the furrow at planting, covered so it does not touch tubers.
entries.summary_rw: Imborera + NPK 17-17-17 ~kg 3 kuri ari (kg 300/ha) mu murongo mu gutera, uyipfuke ntikore ku birayi.
entries.detail_en: Potato needs good fertility. Apply 100-200kg of compost or manure per are before planting. At planting place NPK 17-17-17 at about 3kg per are (300kg/ha) in the furrow and cover with a little soil before placing seed tubers. A split of urea at first hilling can help on poor soils. Confirm rates with your agronomist.
entries.detail_rw: Ibirayi bikenera ubutaka burumbuka. Shyira kg 100-200 by'imborera kuri ari mbere yo gutera. Mu gutera shyira NPK 17-17-17 ~kg 3 kuri ari (kg 300/ha) mu murongo, uyipfukeho agataka mbere yo gushyiraho imbuto. Ure nke ku nshuro ya mbere yo kurunda ishobora gufasha ku butaka bukennye. Baza agronome.

entries.keywords: potato ibirayi late blight mildiou mildiyu leaves black brown spots rain fungicide mancozeb amababi abirabura
entries.summary_en: Dark wet patches on leaves in rainy weather = late blight. Spray an approved preventive fungicide (e.g. mancozeb) every 7-10 days in rains. Use tolerant varieties.
entries.summary_rw: Amabara yijimye kandi atose ku mababi mu gihe cy'imvura ni mildiyu. Tera umuti wemewe (nka mancozeb) buri minsi 7-10 mu mvura. Koresha imbuto zihanganira.
entries.detail_en: Late blight spreads fast in cool, wet weather: brown-black water-soaked patches on leaves, white mould underneath in the morning, dark stem lesions. Prevention: tolerant varieties, certified seed, good spacing, hilling, and removing volunteer potatoes. In rainy periods, spray an RAB-approved protective fungicide (such as mancozeb) every 7-10 days starting before symptoms; use a systemic product only as advised. Wear protective gear and respect the label waiting time before harvest.
entries.detail_rw: Mildiyu yihuta mu gihe cy'imbeho n'imvura: amabara y'ikigina-umukara atose ku mababi, ifu yera munsi y'ibabi mu gitondo, n'ibikomere byijimye ku ruti. Kwirinda: imbuto zihanganira, imbuto zemewe, intera ikwiye, kurunda, no kurandura ibirayi byimejeje. Mu gihe cy'imvura, tera umuti wemejwe na RAB (nka mancozeb) buri minsi 7-10 mbere y'uko ibimenyetso bigaragara. Ambara ibikoresho byo kwirinda kandi wubahirize igihe cyanditse mbere yo gusarura.

entries.keywords: potato ibirayi bacterial wilt wilting ooze tuber rot kuma bagiteri kubora
entries.summary_en: Plants wilt suddenly and cut tubers ooze white liquid: bacterial wilt. No chemical cure: uproot and destroy, use clean seed, rotate 2+ seasons.
entries.summary_rw: Ibirayi biraraba bitunguranye, igirayi ukase kikazana amazi yera: ni indwara ya bagiteri. Nta muti: randura utwike, koresha imbuto nziza, usimburanye ibihembwe 2+.
entries.detail_en: Bacterial wilt: sudden wilting of green plants; a cut tuber shows a brown ring and white bacterial ooze. There is no chemical control. Uproot and destroy affected plants with tubers (do not feed them to animals or leave them in the field). Use certified seed, rotate out of potato, tomato and eggplant for at least 2 seasons, clean tools, and do not let water run from infected plots into clean ones.
entries.detail_rw: Ibirayi bibisi biraraba bitunguranye; igirayi ukase kigaragaza uruziga rw'ikigina n'amazi yera. Nta muti uyivura. Randura ibirayi byanduye n'ibirayi byabyo ubyangize (ntubihe amatungo kandi ntubisige mu murima). Koresha imbuto zemewe, simburanya nibura ibihembwe 2, sukura ibikoresho, kandi ntureke amazi ava mu murima wanduye ajya mu wundi.

entries.keywords: potato ibirayi harvest storage dehaulm skin set store gusarura guhunika
entries.summary_en: Cut the leaves 2 weeks before harvest so skins harden. Harvest in dry weather, sort, and store in a dark, cool, airy place.
entries.summary_rw: Kata amababi ibyumweru 2 mbere yo gusarura kugira ngo igishishwa gikomere. Sarura ku zuba, utoranye, uhunike ahantu h'umwijima, hakonje kandi hafite umwuka.
entries.detail_en: When the crop matures, cut or pull the haulms (leaves and stems) about 2 weeks before harvest so the skin sets and resists bruising. Harvest on a dry day, avoid cutting tubers, and keep them out of the sun (they turn green and toxic). Sort out damaged or rotten tubers. Store ware potatoes in a dark, cool, well-ventilated store; seed potatoes can be kept in diffuse light.
entries.detail_rw: Igihingwa cyeze, kata cyangwa ukure ibibabi n'ibiti ibyumweru 2 mbere yo gusarura kugira ngo igishishwa gikomere. Sarura ku munsi w'izuba, wirinde gukomeretsa ibirayi kandi ntubirekere ku zuba (bihinduka icyatsi bikagira uburozi). Toranya ibyangiritse. Hunika ibirayi byo kurya ahantu h'umwijima, hakonje kandi hinjira umwuka.

entries.keywords: rice umuceri marshland nursery transplanting seedlings spacing water igishanga ipepiniyeri kwimura ingemwe
entries.summary_en: Transplant 21-day seedlings, 2-3 per hill at 20x20cm, in a levelled, puddled field. Keep 3-5cm of water.
entries.summary_rw: Imura ingemwe z'iminsi 21, 2-3 ahantu hamwe kuri cm 20x20, mu murima uringaniye. Gumana amazi ya cm 3-5.
entries.detail_en: Prepare a nursery with certified seed of a variety recommended for your marshland. Plough, puddle and level the field well so water is even. Transplant seedlings at about 21 days, 2-3 seedlings per hill at 20cm x 20cm (straight lines make weeding easier). Keep 3-5cm of water during vegetative growth and drain about 2 weeks before harvest. Coordinate planting dates with your rice cooperative to reduce pests.
entries.detail_rw: Tegura ipepiniyeri ukoresheje imbuto zemewe z'ubwoko bwagenewe igishanga cyawe. Hinga, ucugute kandi uringanize umurima kugira ngo amazi angane. Imura ingemwe zifite iminsi ~21, ingemwe 2-3 ahantu hamwe kuri cm 20 x 20 (imirongo igororotse yorohereza kubagara). Gumana amazi ya cm 3-5 mu gihe cyo gukura, ukureho amazi ibyumweru ~2 mbere yo gusarura. Huza igihe cyo gutera na koperative yawe.

entries.keywords: rice umuceri fertiliser fertilizer NPK urea tillering panicle ifumbire
entries.summary_en: NPK 17-17-17 about 2-2.5kg per are before transplanting; Urea about 1kg per are split at tillering and panicle start.
entries.summary_rw: NPK 17-17-17 ~kg 2-2.5 kuri ari mbere yo kwimura; Ure ~kg 1 kuri ari igabanyijemo kabiri: igihe cyo gushibuka n'igihe cyo kuzana amahundo.
entries.detail_en: Basal: NPK 17-17-17 at about 2-2.5kg per are (200-250kg/ha) incorporated before transplanting. Top-dress Urea at about 1kg per are (100kg/ha) in two splits: at active tillering (about 3 weeks after transplanting) and at panicle initiation. Apply urea into shallow water or moist soil and avoid letting water flow out for a few days. Too much nitrogen increases blast disease. Follow your cooperative's agronomist.
entries.detail_rw: Mbere yo kwimura: NPK 17-17-17 ~kg 2-2.5 kuri ari (kg 200-250/ha) ivanze n'ubutaka. Ure ~kg 1 kuri ari (kg 100/ha) igabanyijemo kabiri: igihe umuceri ushibuka (~ibyumweru 3 nyuma yo kwimura) n'igihe utangiye kuzana amahundo. Shyira ure mu mazi make cyangwa ubutaka butose kandi ntureke amazi asohoka iminsi mike. Azote nyinshi yongera indwara ya bulasite. Kurikiza agronome wa koperative.

entries.keywords: rice umuceri blast diamond spots leaves neck rot panicle white empty grains bulasite amabara
entries.summary_en: Diamond-shaped grey spots on leaves or a rotten neck under the panicle = blast. Use resistant varieties, avoid excess urea, use approved fungicide if advised.
entries.summary_rw: Amabara ameze nka diyama ku mababi cyangwa ijosi ry'ihundo ryaboze ni bulasite. Koresha imbuto zihanganira, wirinde ure nyinshi, umuti wemewe niba ubigiriwemo inama.
entries.detail_en: Blast causes diamond-shaped spots with grey centres on leaves, and 'neck blast' where the stem under the panicle rots and grains stay empty. It is worse at high altitude, with cool nights and heavy nitrogen. Use resistant varieties recommended for your marshland, balanced fertiliser (avoid excess urea), clean seed, and remove infected straw. If neck blast risk is high, an approved fungicide at booting/heading may be advised by your agronomist.
entries.detail_rw: Bulasite itera amabara ameze nka diyama afite hagati h'ibara ry'ivu ku mababi, n'ijosi ry'ihundo ribora impeke zigasigara zirimo ubusa. Iba nyinshi ahantu hirengeye, amajoro akonje na azote nyinshi. Koresha imbuto zihanganira, ifumbire iringaniye (wirinde ure nyinshi), imbuto nziza, ukureho ibyatsi byanduye. Agronome ashobora kukugira inama yo gutera umuti wemewe.

entries.keywords: rice umuceri harvest drying threshing moisture gusarura kumisha guhura
entries.summary_en: Harvest when 80-85% of grains are straw-coloured. Thresh quickly and dry on tarpaulins to 14% moisture before storing.
entries.summary_rw: Sarura iyo 80-85% by'impeke zahindutse umuhondo w'ibyatsi. Hura vuba unanike kuri shitingi kugeza byumye neza mbere yo guhunika.
entries.detail_en: Drain the field about 2 weeks before harvest. Harvest when 80-85% of grains are straw-coloured; late harvest causes shattering and cracked grains. Thresh within 1-2 days, on tarpaulins not bare ground, and dry to 14% moisture. Store clean and dry in bags on pallets. Delivering through your cooperative gives better prices from mills.
entries.detail_rw: Kuraho amazi mu murima ibyumweru ~2 mbere yo gusarura. Sarura iyo 80-85% by'impeke byahindutse umuhondo w'ibyatsi; gutinda bituma impeke zihungura kandi zivunika. Hura mu minsi 1-2, kuri shitingi si ku butaka, unanike kugeza ku bushuhe bwa 14%. Hunika bisukuye kandi byumye mu mifuka iri ku mbaho. Kugurisha binyuze muri koperative bitanga igiciro cyiza.

entries.keywords: cassava imyumbati cuttings stakes planting spacing ingeri gutera intera
entries.summary_en: Use healthy cuttings 20-25cm long from certified, disease-free plants. Plant at 1m x 1m, slanting, two-thirds in the soil.
entries.summary_rw: Koresha ingeri nzima za cm 20-25 ziva ku myumbati yemewe itarwaye. Tera kuri m 1 x 1, ziberamye, bibiri bya gatatu biri mu butaka.
entries.detail_en: Use cuttings from certified, disease-resistant varieties released by RAB (mosaic and brown streak resistant). Take cuttings 20-25cm long with 5-7 nodes from mature stems (8-18 months old) of healthy plants. Plant at 1m x 1m, slanting or vertical, with two-thirds in the soil. Weed during the first 3 months. Cassava can be intercropped with beans in the first months.
entries.detail_rw: Koresha ingeri z'ubwoko bwemewe na RAB buhanganira indwara (ububembe n'indwara y'imirongo y'ikigina). Fata ingeri za cm 20-25 zifite amapfundo 5-7 ku biti bikuze (amezi 8-18) by'imyumbati nzima. Tera kuri m 1 x 1, ziberamye cyangwa zihagaze, bibiri bya gatatu biri mu butaka. Bagara mu mezi 3 ya mbere. Ushobora guhinga ibishyimbo hagati mu mezi ya mbere.

entries.title_en: Cassava mosaic and brown streak disease
entries.keywords: cassava imyumbati mosaic CMD brown streak CBSD virus whitefly yellow leaves distorted root rot ububembe imirongo amababi
entries.summary_en: Yellow-green twisted leaves = mosaic; brown streaks on stems and rotten brown roots = brown streak. Uproot sick plants early and use clean cuttings of resistant varieties.
entries.summary_rw: Amababi y'umuhondo n'icyatsi yihinnye ni ububembe; imirongo y'ikigina ku biti n'ibijumba byaboze ni indwara y'imirongo. Randura imyumbati irwaye kare, ukoreshe ingeri nzima.
entries.detail_en: Both are virus diseases spread by whiteflies and by planting infected cuttings. Mosaic (CMD): leaves mottled yellow-green, twisted and small. Brown streak (CBSD): yellow patches on leaves, brown streaks on stems, and dry brown rot inside roots. No chemical cure. Control: plant only clean cuttings of resistant varieties, uproot and destroy sick plants in the first 3 months (roguing), and do not take cuttings from fields with symptoms.
entries.detail_rw: Zombi ni indwara ziterwa na virusi zikwirakwizwa n'udusimba twera (whiteflies) n'ingeri zanduye. Ububembe: amababi afite amabara y'umuhondo n'icyatsi, yihinnye kandi mato. Indwara y'imirongo y'ikigina: amabara y'umuhondo ku mababi, imirongo y'ikigina ku biti, n'ibijumba biboze imbere. Nta muti. Kurwanya: tera ingeri nzima z'ubwoko buhanganira, randura imyumbati irwaye mu mezi 3 ya mbere, kandi ntufate ingeri mu murima urwaye.

entries.keywords: cassava imyumbati harvest processing drying flour cyanide gusarura kumisha ifu
entries.summary_en: Harvest from 9-18 months as needed. Roots spoil in 2-3 days: peel, soak or dry quickly. Process bitter varieties well to remove cyanide.
entries.summary_rw: Sarura kuva ku mezi 9-18 uko ubikeneye. Ibijumba byangirika mu minsi 2-3: hata, winike cyangwa wumishe vuba. Tunganya neza imyumbati isharira.
entries.detail_en: Cassava is ready from about 9-18 months depending on variety. Harvest only what you can use or sell within 2 days, because fresh roots spoil fast. Peel, chop and sun-dry on clean tarpaulins or raised racks, or soak (fermentation) before drying. Bitter varieties must be well processed (soaking and drying) to remove cyanide before eating.
entries.detail_rw: Imyumbati yera hagati y'amezi 9-18 bitewe n'ubwoko. Sarura ibyo ushobora gukoresha cyangwa kugurisha mu minsi 2, kuko ibijumba bibisi byangirika vuba. Hata, ukatagure, wanike kuri shitingi zisukuye cyangwa ku rutara, cyangwa winike mbere yo kumisha. Imyumbati isharira igomba gutunganywa neza (kwinika no kumisha) kugira ngo uburozi buveho mbere yo kuribwa.

entries.keywords: banana urutoki insina kirabiranya xanthomonas wilt BXW yellow ooze male bud premature ripening ibitoki kuma
entries.summary_en: Yellowing, wilting, early ripening and yellow ooze when cut = Kirabiranya. Remove male buds with a forked stick, disinfect tools, uproot sick mats.
entries.summary_rw: Amababi y'umuhondo, kuma, ibitoki byera imburagihe n'amazi y'umuhondo iyo ukase ni Kirabiranya. Kura ikimenyetso cy'umugabo ukoresheje igiti gifite amashami, sukura ibikoresho, randura insina zirwaye.
entries.detail_en: Kirabiranya (BXW) is a bacterial disease with no chemical cure. Signs: leaves yellow and wilt, the male bud shrivels, fruits ripen early and unevenly, and cut stems ooze yellow liquid. It spreads through insects visiting male flowers, dirty tools, and infected suckers. Control: remove the male bud with a forked stick once the last hand forms; disinfect knives with fire or bleach between plants; cut down and bury or burn sick plants (single stem removal or whole mat); plant clean suckers; report to your sector agronomist.
entries.detail_rw: Kirabiranya ni indwara iterwa na bagiteri idafite umuti. Ibimenyetso: amababi ahinduka umuhondo akuma, umwanana w'urutoki (ikimenyetso cy'umugabo) urumirana, ibitoki byera imburagihe, n'uruti rukase ruzana amazi y'umuhondo. Ikwirakwizwa n'udukoko, ibikoresho byanduye n'insina zanduye. Kurwanya: kura ikimenyetso cy'umugabo ukoresheje igiti gifite amashami; sukura umuhoro ukoresheje umuriro cyangwa javeli; tema insina zirwaye uzitabe cyangwa uzitwike; tera insina nzima; menyesha agronome w'umurenge.

entries.title_rw: Urutoki: gutera no kwita ku rutoki
entries.keywords: banana urutoki insina planting spacing suckers mulch desuckering weevil gutera intera ibisigazwa gusasira
entries.summary_en: Plant clean suckers at 3m x 3m in holes 60cm deep with manure. Keep 3 plants per mat, mulch heavily, and remove old leaves.
entries.summary_rw: Tera insina nzima kuri m 3 x 3 mu myobo ya cm 60 irimo imborera. Siga insina 3 ku gihuru, usasire cyane, ukureho amababi ashaje.
entries.detail_en: Use clean suckers (or tissue-culture plantlets) from disease-free fields. Dig holes 60x60x60cm, mix topsoil with 20kg of manure, and plant at 3m x 3m. Keep only 3 plants per mat (mother, daughter, granddaughter) by removing extra suckers. Mulch with crop residues to keep moisture and add manure each season. Remove dry leaves and keep the base clean to reduce banana weevils.
entries.detail_rw: Koresha ingemwe nzima cyangwa izakozwe muri laboratwari ziva mu mirima itarwaye. Cukura imyobo ya cm 60x60x60, uvange itaka ryo hejuru na kg 20 z'imborera, utere kuri m 3 x 3. Siga insina 3 gusa ku gihuru (nyina, umukobwa, umwuzukuru). Sasira ukoresheje ibisigazwa by'imyaka kugira ngo ubutaka bugumane ubuhehere, wongereho imborera buri gihembwe. Kuraho amababi yumye kandi usukure hasi kugira ngo ugabanye ibivumvuri.

entries.keywords: banana urutoki fertiliser fertilizer manure mulch potassium ifumbire gusasira
entries.summary_en: Give each mat 10-20kg of manure or compost per season and keep a thick mulch. Bananas need lots of potassium: return peels and stems to the field.
entries.summary_rw: Ha buri gihuru kg 10-20 z'imborera buri gihembwe kandi usasire cyane. Urutoki rukenera potasiyumu nyinshi: subiza ibishishwa n'ibitumbwe mu murima.
entries.detail_en: Bananas respond best to organic matter. Apply 10-20kg of well-decomposed manure or compost per mat each season, spread around the mat (not against the stem). Keep a thick mulch of grass or crop residues. Chop and return pseudostems after harvest (except from diseased plants). Where available and advised, NPK or potassium fertiliser increases bunch size.
entries.detail_rw: Urutoki rukenera cyane ifumbire y'imborera. Shyira kg 10-20 z'imborera iboze neza ku gihuru buri gihembwe, uyikwirakwize hirya no hino (si ku gitumbwe). Sasira cyane ukoresheje ibyatsi cyangwa ibisigazwa. Tema ibitumbwe nyuma yo gusarura ubisubize mu murima (keretse ibirwaye). Aho bishoboka, NPK cyangwa ifumbire ya potasiyumu byongera ubunini bw'igitoki.

entries.title_en: Coffee: antestia bug and leaf rust
entries.keywords: coffee ikawa antestia bug potato taste defect leaf rust orange powder pests ingese udusimba
entries.summary_en: Antestia bugs cause the 'potato taste' defect: prune for open bushes, hand-pick, and follow NAEB spraying advice. Orange powder under leaves is rust.
entries.summary_rw: Antestiya itera uburyohe bw'ibirayi mu ikawa: konora ibiti, utore udusimba, ukurikize inama za NAEB. Ifu y'icunga munsi y'amababi ni ingese.
entries.detail_en: Antestia bugs (shield-shaped, black-orange) damage berries and are linked to the 'potato taste' defect that lowers Rwandan coffee prices. Keep bushes open by pruning, hand-collect bugs in the morning, and use treatments only as advised by NAEB. Leaf rust: orange powdery spots under leaves, leaf drop; use resistant varieties, good nutrition and NAEB-recommended fungicides. Pick only ripe red cherries and deliver them to the washing station the same day.
entries.detail_rw: Udusimba twa antestiya (dufite ishusho y'ingabo, umukara n'icunga) twangiza imbuto kandi dutera uburyohe bw'ibirayi bugabanya igiciro cy'ikawa y'u Rwanda. Konora ibiti kugira ngo bifunguke, tora udusimba mu gitondo, ukoreshe imiti gusa ukurikije inama za NAEB. Ingese: amabara y'ifu y'icunga munsi y'amababi, amababi agahunguka; koresha ubwoko buhanganira, ifumbire ikwiye n'imiti NAEB yemeza. Sarura imbuto zihishije zitukura gusa, uzigeze ku ruganda uwo munsi.

entries.keywords: coffee ikawa fertiliser fertilizer mulch pruning NAEB ifumbire gusasira konora
entries.summary_en: Mulch coffee heavily, apply manure, and use the fertiliser supplied or recommended by NAEB. Prune after harvest to keep productive stems.
entries.summary_rw: Sasira ikawa cyane, ushyireho imborera, ukoreshe ifumbire itangwa cyangwa yemejwe na NAEB. Konora nyuma yo gusarura.
entries.detail_en: Coffee needs mulch to protect soil moisture, especially in Eastern and Southern districts. Apply manure or compost around the drip line, and use the mineral fertiliser supplied or recommended by NAEB at the advised rate and timing. Prune after harvest: remove old, dry and unproductive stems and excess suckers to keep 2-4 productive stems per tree.
entries.detail_rw: Ikawa ikenera gusasirwa kugira ngo ubutaka bugumane ubuhehere, cyane cyane mu turere tw'Iburasirazuba n'Amajyepfo. Shyira imborera ku ruziga rw'amababi, ukoreshe ifumbire mvaruganda itangwa cyangwa yemejwe na NAEB ku rugero n'igihe byagenwe. Konora nyuma yo gusarura: kuraho ibiti bishaje, byumye n'ibidatanga umusaruro.

entries.keywords: coffee ikawa harvest cherries red washing station quality gusarura uruganda
entries.summary_en: Pick only ripe red cherries, keep them in clean bags out of the sun, and deliver to the washing station the same day.
entries.summary_rw: Sarura imbuto zihishije zitukura gusa, uzibike mu mifuka isukuye itari ku zuba, uzigeze ku ruganda rutunganya ikawa uwo munsi.
entries.detail_en: Quality is made at harvest. Pick only fully ripe red cherries; green or overripe cherries lower the grade. Do not mix fallen or damaged cherries. Keep cherries in clean bags in the shade and deliver to the washing station the same day (fermentation starts within hours). Selling through your cooperative or washing station gives traceability and better prices.
entries.detail_rw: Ubwiza bw'ikawa butangirira mu isarura. Sarura imbuto zihishije neza zitukura gusa; izitarera cyangwa izarenze zigabanya agaciro. Ntuvange imbuto zaguye hasi cyangwa zangiritse. Zibike mu mifuka isukuye mu gicucu, uzigeze ku ruganda uwo munsi. Kugurisha binyuze muri koperative bitanga igiciro cyiza.

entries.keywords: cattle cow dairy inka feeding napier grass fodder water milk minerals urubingo ubwatsi amazi amata kugaburira umunyu
entries.summary_en: A dairy cow needs about 10% of its weight in fresh fodder daily, 50-100 litres of clean water, mineral salt, and legumes like calliandra or desmodium.
entries.summary_rw: Inka y'amata ikenera ubwatsi bubisi bungana na 10% by'ibiro byayo ku munsi, litiro 50-100 z'amazi meza, umunyu w'amatungo, n'ibinyamisogwe nka kaliyandra.
entries.detail_en: Feed a dairy cow about 10% of its body weight in fresh fodder daily (40-50kg for a 450kg cow). Napier grass (urubingo) cut at about 1m tall is most nutritious. Mix in legumes such as calliandra, leucaena or desmodium for protein. Provide clean water at all times (50-100 litres a day, more when milking), and a mineral lick. Concentrates (e.g. maize bran) improve milk yield for high producers. Make hay or silage in the rainy season for the dry season.
entries.detail_rw: Gaburira inka y'amata ubwatsi bubisi bungana na ~10% by'ibiro byayo ku munsi (kg 40-50 ku nka ya kg 450). Urubingo rutemwe rufite nka m 1 ni rwo rufite intungamubiri nyinshi. Vangamo ibinyamisogwe nka kaliyandra, lusina cyangwa desimodiyumu. Ha inka amazi meza igihe cyose (litiro 50-100 ku munsi), n'umunyu w'amatungo. Ibiryo byongera umusaruro (nk'ibisigazwa by'ibigori) byongera amata. Bika ubwatsi (hay/silage) mu gihe cy'imvura uzakoresha mu cyi.

entries.title_en: Ticks and East Coast Fever in cattle
entries.title_rw: Uburondwe n'indwara ya East Coast Fever mu nka
entries.keywords: cattle cow inka ticks east coast fever ECF swollen lymph nodes fever acaricide spray dip uburondwe umuriro guhumeka kwoza
entries.summary_en: Spray or dip cattle against ticks regularly with an approved acaricide. Fever, swollen glands near the ear/shoulder and fast breathing can be East Coast Fever: call a vet immediately.
entries.summary_rw: Oza inka imiti yica uburondwe buri gihe. Umuriro, imitsi yabyimbye hafi y'ugutwi/urutugu no guhumeka vuba bishobora kuba East Coast Fever: hamagara veterineri vuba.
entries.detail_en: East Coast Fever is spread by the brown ear tick and kills many cattle, especially exotic breeds and calves. Signs: high fever, swollen lymph nodes in front of the shoulder and below the ear, fast breathing, frothy nose discharge, reduced milk. Prevention: spray or dip with an approved acaricide on a regular schedule (often weekly in high-risk areas), check ears and tail for ticks, and ask your vet about ECF vaccination (ITM). Treatment must be given early by a veterinarian.
entries.detail_rw: East Coast Fever ikwirakwizwa n'uburondwe bwo ku matwi kandi yica inka nyinshi, cyane cyane iz'amahanga n'inyana. Ibimenyetso: umuriro mwinshi, imitsi yabyimbye imbere y'urutugu no munsi y'ugutwi, guhumeka vuba, ibimyira bifite urufuro, amata agabanuka. Kwirinda: oza cyangwa utere inka umuti wemewe wica uburondwe buri gihe (akenshi buri cyumweru ahari ibyago byinshi), genzura amatwi n'umurizo, ubaze veterineri ku rukingo. Ivurwa hakiri kare na veterineri.

entries.keywords: cattle cow inka mastitis udder swollen milk clots blood hygiene milking amabere amata
entries.summary_en: Hot, swollen udder or clots/blood in milk = mastitis. Milk with clean hands, wash and dry teats, milk sick quarters last, and call a vet for treatment.
entries.summary_rw: Amabere ashyushye, yabyimbye, cyangwa amata arimo ibibumbe/amaraso ni mastite. Kama n'intoki zisukuye, ozwa unumishe amabere, ukame iryanduye nyuma, uhamagare veterineri.
entries.detail_en: Mastitis is infection of the udder. Signs: udder hot, swollen or painful; milk watery, with clots, pus or blood. Prevention: clean, dry housing; wash hands; clean and dry teats before milking; milk completely; dip teats after milking where possible; milk infected cows last. Treatment requires antibiotics prescribed by a vet; do not sell milk during the withdrawal period.
entries.detail_rw: Mastite ni indwara y'amabere. Ibimenyetso: amabere ashyushye, yabyimbye cyangwa ababara; amata ameze nk'amazi, arimo ibibumbe, amashyira cyangwa amaraso. Kwirinda: ikiraro gisukuye kandi cyumye; karaba intoki; sukura unumishe amabere mbere yo gukama; kama amata yose; kama inka irwaye nyuma. Kuvurwa bisaba imiti yandikwa na veterineri; ntugurishe amata mu gihe cyagenwe nyuma y'imiti.

entries.keywords: cattle cow inka foot and mouth disease FMD uburenge blisters mouth feet drooling lameness quarantine ibisebe
entries.summary_en: Blisters in the mouth and feet, drooling and limping = possible Uburenge. Do not move or sell animals; report to the sector vet immediately.
entries.summary_rw: Ibisebe mu kanwa no ku nzara, inkonda nyinshi no gucumbagira bishobora kuba uburenge. Ntimwimure cyangwa ngo mugurishe amatungo; menyesha veterineri w'umurenge vuba.
entries.detail_en: Foot-and-mouth disease (Uburenge) is a notifiable, highly contagious disease of cattle, goats, sheep and pigs. Signs: fever, blisters in the mouth, on the tongue, feet and teats, heavy drooling, lameness, sharp drop in milk. Action: isolate sick animals, stop all movement and sales, keep visitors away, and report immediately to the sector veterinarian. Vaccination campaigns are organised by RAB.
entries.detail_rw: Uburenge ni indwara yandura cyane igomba kumenyeshwa, ifata inka, ihene, intama n'ingurube. Ibimenyetso: umuriro, ibisebe mu kanwa, ku rurimi, ku nzara no ku mabere, inkonda nyinshi, gucumbagira, amata akagabanuka cyane. Icyo gukora: tandukanya amatungo arwaye, hagarika kwimura no kugurisha, ntureke abashyitsi binjira, umenyeshe veterineri w'umurenge vuba. Inkingo zitangwa na RAB.

entries.keywords: chicken poultry inkoko newcastle muryamo vaccination twisted neck diarrhoea death sudden urukingo
entries.summary_en: Many chickens dying fast with twisted necks, green diarrhoea or breathing problems = possible Newcastle. Vaccinate every 3 months; isolate sick birds; tell the vet.
entries.summary_rw: Inkoko nyinshi zipfa vuba, amajosi yihinnye, impiswi y'icyatsi cyangwa guhumeka nabi bishobora kuba muryamo. Kingira buri mezi 3; tandukanya izirwaye; menyesha veterineri.
entries.detail_en: Newcastle disease can kill a whole flock in days. Signs: sudden deaths, gasping and coughing, green watery diarrhoea, twisted neck, paralysis, drop in eggs. There is no treatment. Prevention: vaccinate all birds regularly (commonly every 3 months, with a thermostable vaccine for village chickens), isolate new birds for 2 weeks, keep the house clean, and limit visitors. Bury or burn dead birds and report outbreaks.
entries.detail_rw: Muryamo ishobora kwica inkoko zose mu minsi mike. Ibimenyetso: gupfa gutunguranye, gukorora no guhumeka nabi, impiswi y'icyatsi, ijosi ryihinnye, kumugara, amagi akagabanuka. Nta muti. Kwirinda: kingira inkoko zose buri gihe (akenshi buri mezi 3), tandukanya inkoko nshya ibyumweru 2, sukura inzu y'inkoko, ugabanye abasura. Taba cyangwa utwike inkoko zapfuye, umenyeshe veterineri.

entries.keywords: chicken poultry inkoko feed layers broilers housing water eggs ibiryo amazi amagi inzu
entries.summary_en: Give clean water always, balanced feed for the bird type (chick, grower, layer), and a dry, airy, clean house with about 4-5 birds per square metre.
entries.summary_rw: Ha inkoko amazi meza igihe cyose, ibiryo bikwiranye n'ikigero cyazo, n'inzu yumye, ihumeka kandi isukuye: inkoko 4-5 kuri m2.
entries.detail_en: Provide clean water at all times; a laying hen drinks about 250ml a day. Feed the right ration for the stage: chick mash (0-8 weeks), grower (8-18 weeks), layer mash (from first egg). Village chickens benefit from extra kitchen scraps, maize bran and greens. House: dry, well-ventilated, rain-proof, about 4-5 adult birds per square metre, with clean litter and nest boxes.
entries.detail_rw: Ha amazi meza igihe cyose; inkoko itera amagi inywa ~ml 250 ku munsi. Gaburira ibiryo bikwiranye n'ikigero: ibiryo by'imishwi (ibyumweru 0-8), by'inkoko zikura (ibyumweru 8-18), n'iby'inkoko zitera (guhera ku igi rya mbere). Inkoko za gakondo zungukira ku bisigazwa byo mu gikoni, umurama n'imboga. Inzu: yumye, ihumeka neza, itava, inkoko nkuru 4-5 kuri m2, irimo ibyatsi bisukuye n'aho gutera.

entries.title_en: Pigs: African swine fever and biosecurity
entries.title_rw: Ingurube: African Swine Fever no kwirinda indwara
entries.keywords: pig pigs ingurube african swine fever ASF death red skin fever biosecurity swill kwirinda
entries.summary_en: Pigs dying with fever and red/purple skin may be African swine fever: no vaccine or cure. Stop movement, report to the vet, never feed uncooked swill.
entries.summary_rw: Ingurube zipfa zifite umuriro n'uruhu rutukura/rw'isine bishobora kuba ASF: nta rukingo cyangwa umuti. Hagarika kwimura, menyesha veterineri, ntugaburire ibisigazwa bidatetse.
entries.detail_en: African swine fever (ASF) kills most infected pigs. Signs: high fever, not eating, red or purple patches on ears, belly and legs, sudden deaths. There is no vaccine or treatment. Biosecurity: keep pigs confined, do not buy pigs of unknown origin, boil kitchen swill before feeding, use dedicated boots and a footbath, and limit visitors. If you suspect ASF, stop all movement and sales and report to the sector vet.
entries.detail_rw: ASF yica ingurube nyinshi zanduye. Ibimenyetso: umuriro mwinshi, kwanga kurya, amabara atukura cyangwa y'isine ku matwi, ku nda no ku maguru, gupfa gutunguranye. Nta rukingo cyangwa umuti. Kwirinda: fungirana ingurube, ntugure ingurube utazi aho zivuye, teka ibisigazwa mbere yo kubigaburira, koresha inkweto zabigenewe, ugabanye abasura. Niba ukeka ASF, hagarika kwimura no kugurisha, umenyeshe veterineri w'umurenge.

entries.keywords: pig pigs ingurube feeding feed housing sty water ibiryo inzu amazi
entries.summary_en: Feed pigs a balanced ration (bran, legumes, greens, minerals), give plenty of clean water, and keep them in a clean, dry, roofed sty.
entries.summary_rw: Gaburira ingurube ibiryo biringaniye (umurama, ibinyamisogwe, imboga, imyunyu), uzihe amazi meza menshi, uzibike mu kiraro gisukuye, cyumye kandi gisakaye.
entries.detail_en: Pigs grow well on a balanced diet: energy (maize bran, cassava), protein (soybean, fish meal, legumes), greens (sweet potato vines) and minerals. Always cook kitchen swill to prevent disease. Provide plenty of clean water. House pigs in a roofed, dry sty with a sloping concrete or well-drained floor; clean daily. Deworm every 3 months as advised by a vet.
entries.detail_rw: Ingurube zikura neza iyo zigaburiwe indyo iringaniye: ibitera imbaraga (umurama, imyumbati), poroteyine (soya, ifu y'amafi, ibinyamisogwe), imboga (imigozi y'ibijumba) n'imyunyu. Teka ibisigazwa byo mu gikoni buri gihe. Ha ingurube amazi meza menshi. Ziba mu kiraro gisakaye, cyumye, gifite hasi hahanamye; sukura buri munsi. Zihe imiti y'inzoka buri mezi 3 ukurikije inama ya veterineri.

entries.keywords: goat goats ihene sheep intama feeding housing deworming worms kugaburira inzoka
entries.summary_en: Give goats browse and legume leaves, clean water and minerals; house them on a raised slatted floor; deworm every 3-4 months as advised by a vet.
entries.summary_rw: Gaburira ihene amababi y'ibiti n'ibinyamisogwe, amazi meza n'umunyu; zibe mu kiraro gifite hasi hazamuye; zihe imiti y'inzoka buri mezi 3-4.
entries.detail_en: Goats prefer browse (leaves of shrubs and trees such as calliandra and leucaena) mixed with grasses. Provide clean water and a mineral lick. House goats on a raised slatted floor to keep them dry and reduce worms and foot problems. Deworm every 3-4 months or as advised by a vet, trim hooves, and separate sick animals.
entries.detail_rw: Ihene zikunda amababi y'ibiti n'ibihuru (nka kaliyandra na lusina) avanze n'ubwatsi. Ha ihene amazi meza n'umunyu w'amatungo. Zibe mu kiraro gifite hasi hazamuye kugira ngo zigume zumye, bigabanye inzoka n'indwara z'ibinono. Zihe imiti y'inzoka buri mezi 3-4 cyangwa nk'uko veterineri abigira inama, uzikate inzara, utandukanye izirwaye.

entries.keywords: soil ubutaka acidity acid lime ishwagara travertine compost manure fertility soil test uburumbuke
entries.summary_en: Many Rwandan highland soils are acidic. Apply lime (ishwagara) where a soil test or agronomist advises, plus compost every season, to make fertiliser work.
entries.summary_rw: Ubutaka bwinshi bw'imisozi y'u Rwanda burasharira. Shyiramo ishwagara aho isuzuma ry'ubutaka cyangwa agronome abigira inama, n'imborera buri gihembwe.
entries.detail_en: Acidic soils lock up nutrients so fertiliser gives poor results; beans and maize suffer most. Where a soil test or your agronomist recommends it, apply agricultural lime (ishwagara/travertine) 2-4 weeks before planting and mix it into the soil; rates are often 1.5-2.5 t/ha. Add compost or manure every season to build organic matter. Ask your sector agronomist about soil testing and subsidised lime through Smart Nkunganire.
entries.detail_rw: Ubutaka busharira bufunga intungamubiri, bityo ifumbire ntitange umusaruro; ibishyimbo n'ibigori ni byo bibabara cyane. Aho isuzuma ry'ubutaka cyangwa agronome abigira inama, shyiramo ishwagara ibyumweru 2-4 mbere yo gutera uyivange n'ubutaka; akenshi ni toni 1.5-2.5/ha. Ongeramo imborera buri gihembwe. Baza agronome w'umurenge ku isuzuma ry'ubutaka n'ishwagara inyuze muri Nkunganire.

entries.keywords: compost manure organic matter making heap ifumbire imborera ikirundo
entries.summary_en: Layer dry plant material, green material, manure and a little soil; keep moist; turn every 2-3 weeks. Ready in about 2-3 months.
entries.summary_rw: Rundanya ibyatsi byumye, ibibisi, amase n'agataka, ubyuhire; ubihindure buri byumweru 2-3. Biba byabaye ifumbire mu mezi 2-3.
entries.detail_en: Choose a shaded spot or pit. Build layers: dry material (straw, maize stalks), green material (weeds, leaves), animal manure, and a thin layer of soil or ash; repeat to about 1-1.5m. Keep moist like a squeezed sponge, cover against rain, and turn the heap every 2-3 weeks. Compost is ready in 2-3 months when dark, crumbly and earthy-smelling.
entries.detail_rw: Hitamo ahantu h'igicucu cyangwa icyobo. Rundanya: ibyatsi byumye (ibikenyeri, ibigorigori), ibyatsi bibisi, amase, n'agataka cyangwa ivu; usubiremo kugeza kuri m 1-1.5. Gumana ubuhehere nk'eponje ikamuwe, upfuke imvura, uhindure ikirundo buri byumweru 2-3. Ifumbire iba yeze mu mezi 2-3 iyo yirabura, ivungagurika kandi ihumura nk'ubutaka.

entries.keywords: erosion isuri terraces hillside slope contour grass strips trenches amaterasi imirwanyasuri imisozi
entries.summary_en: On slopes, use terraces or contour lines with grass strips and trenches, mulch, and agroforestry trees to stop soil and fertiliser washing away.
entries.summary_rw: Ku misozi, koresha amaterasi cyangwa imirwanyasuri iteyeho ubwatsi, gusasira n'ibiti bivangwa n'imyaka kugira ngo ubutaka n'ifumbire bitatwarwa n'isuri.
entries.detail_en: Heavy rains wash away topsoil and fertiliser on Rwanda's slopes. Build terraces (radical or progressive) or contour trenches; plant grass strips such as napier or vetiver along contours (which also feed livestock); keep the soil covered with mulch or cover crops; and plant agroforestry trees (grevillea, calliandra) along boundaries. Ask your sector about community terracing programmes.
entries.detail_rw: Imvura nyinshi itwara ubutaka bwo hejuru n'ifumbire ku misozi y'u Rwanda. Kora amaterasi y'indinganire cyangwa imirwanyasuri; tera ubwatsi nk'urubingo cyangwa vetiveri ku mirwanyasuri (bugaburira n'amatungo); pfuka ubutaka ukoresheje gusasira; utere ibiti bivangwa n'imyaka (gereviliya, kaliyandra). Baza umurenge ku bikorwa by'amaterasi.

entries.keywords: pesticide pesticides safety spray protective equipment label waiting period approved list imiti yica udukoko kwirinda gutera
entries.summary_en: Use only RAB-approved products from licensed agro-dealers. Read the label, wear gloves, mask and boots, never spray in wind, respect the waiting time before harvest.
entries.summary_rw: Koresha imiti yemejwe na RAB iva ku bacuruzi bemewe. Soma ibyanditse, wambare gants, agapfukamunwa n'inkweto, ntuterere mu muyaga, wubahirize igihe mbere yo gusarura.
entries.detail_en: Buy only products on the RAB-approved list from licensed agro-dealers, in sealed, labelled containers. Read and follow the label dose. Wear gloves, a mask, long sleeves and boots; do not eat, drink or smoke while spraying; do not spray in wind or before rain. Respect the pre-harvest interval on the label. Store pesticides locked away from food, children and animals, and never reuse containers for water or food.
entries.detail_rw: Gura imiti iri ku rutonde rwemejwe na RAB gusa, ku bacuruzi bemewe, mu bikoresho bifunze kandi byanditseho. Soma ukurikize urugero rwanditse. Ambara gants, agapfukamunwa, imyenda ndende n'inkweto; ntukarye, ntunywe cyangwa ngo unywe itabi utera umuti; ntuterere mu muyaga cyangwa mbere y'imvura. Ubahirize igihe cyanditse mbere yo gusarura. Bika imiti ifungiranye kure y'ibiryo, abana n'amatungo, kandi ntuzongere gukoresha ibikoresho byayo.
entries.source: RAB; FAO International Code of Conduct on Pesticide Management

entries.keywords: subsidy subsidised inputs smart nkunganire SNS agro-dealer seed fertiliser register nkunganire inyongeramusaruro nkunganire
entries.summary_en: Register through your village/cell and the Smart Nkunganire System (SNS), then buy seed and fertiliser at a subsidised price from a registered agro-dealer.
entries.summary_rw: Iyandikishe binyuze mu mudugudu/akagari no muri Smart Nkunganire (SNS), hanyuma ugure imbuto n'ifumbire ku giciro cyunganiwe ku mucuruzi wemewe.
entries.detail_en: Rwanda's Smart Nkunganire System (SNS) lets farmers buy seed, fertiliser and lime at a government-subsidised price. Register your land and crop plan with your village/cell agronomist or farmer promoter before the season, then order and buy from a registered agro-dealer near you. Ask your sector agronomist for current prices and deadlines for the coming season.
entries.detail_rw: Smart Nkunganire (SNS) ifasha abahinzi kugura imbuto, ifumbire n'ishwagara ku giciro cyunganiwe na Leta. Iyandikishe n'ubutaka n'igihingwa uteganya ku mujyanama w'ubuhinzi w'akagari cyangwa umuhinzi mworozi w'icyitegererezo mbere y'igihembwe, hanyuma utumize kandi ugure ku mucuruzi wemewe ukwegereye. Baza agronome w'umurenge ibiciro n'amatariki y'igihembwe gitaha.

entries.keywords: drought dry spell climate smart mulching water harvesting drought tolerant varieties irrigation amapfa izuba gusasira kubika amazi kuhira imihindagurikire
entries.summary_en: Mulch to keep moisture, harvest rainwater, use early-maturing or drought-tolerant varieties, and plant at the first reliable rains.
entries.summary_rw: Sasira kugira ngo ubutaka bugumane ubuhehere, fata amazi y'imvura, koresha imbuto zera vuba cyangwa zihanganira izuba, kandi utere imvura ya mbere imaze gukomera.
entries.detail_en: Dry spells are increasing, especially in Eastern Province. Practices that help: mulching with crop residues; rainwater harvesting (roof tanks, farm ponds, trenches); planting early-maturing or drought-tolerant varieties; intercropping and agroforestry; small-scale irrigation where available; and planting at the onset of reliable rains rather than after the first shower. Keep some fodder and seed in reserve.
entries.detail_rw: Amapfa ariyongera, cyane cyane mu Ntara y'Iburasirazuba. Ibifasha: gusasira ukoresheje ibisigazwa by'imyaka; gufata amazi y'imvura (ibigega, ibyuzi, imirwanyasuri); gutera imbuto zera vuba cyangwa zihanganira izuba; kuvanga imyaka n'ibiti; kuhira aho bishoboka; no gutera imvura imaze gukomera aho gutera nyuma y'imvura ya mbere. Bika ubwatsi n'imbuto zo kwifashisha.

entries.keywords: season seasons calendar season A season B season C when to plant igihembwe ihinga kalendari igihe cyo gutera
entries.summary_en: Season A: Sept-Jan (plant Sept-Oct). Season B: Feb-June (plant Feb-Mar). Season C: June-Sept in marshlands with irrigation.
entries.summary_rw: Igihembwe A: Nzeri-Mutarama (tera Nzeri-Ukwakira). Igihembwe B: Gashyantare-Kamena (tera Gashyantare-Werurwe). Igihembwe C: Kamena-Nzeri mu bishanga byuhirwa.
entries.detail_en: Rwanda has two main rainy seasons. Season A runs from September to January, with planting in September-October. Season B runs from February to June, with planting in February-March. Season C (June-September) is the dry season, used for marshland and irrigated crops such as vegetables and beans. Exact dates vary by district and year, so check the weather forecast and your sector's crop calendar.
entries.detail_rw: U Rwanda rufite ibihe bibiri by'imvura. Igihembwe A kiva muri Nzeri kugeza muri Mutarama, gutera biba muri Nzeri-Ukwakira. Igihembwe B kiva muri Gashyantare kugeza muri Kamena, gutera biba muri Gashyantare-Werurwe. Igihembwe C (Kamena-Nzeri) ni icyi, gikoreshwa mu bishanga n'ahuhirwa. Amatariki ahinduka bitewe n'akarere n'umwaka; reba iteganyagihe na kalendari y'umurenge.

entries.keywords: help extension officer agronomist vet veterinarian farmer promoter twigire muhinzi contact ubufasha agronome veterineri umujyanama
entries.summary_en: For field visits ask your village farmer promoter (Twigire Muhinzi), cell/sector agronomist, or sector veterinarian for animals.
entries.summary_rw: Ku bufasha bwo mu murima baza umuhinzi mworozi w'icyitegererezo (Twigire Muhinzi), agronome w'akagari/umurenge, cyangwa veterineri w'umurenge ku matungo.
entries.detail_en: Under Twigire Muhinzi, every village has farmer promoters and Farmer Field School facilitators who can visit your farm. For crop problems contact your cell or sector agronomist; for animal health contact the sector veterinarian. Report outbreaks of pests or animal diseases quickly so they can be contained.
entries.detail_rw: Muri gahunda ya Twigire Muhinzi, buri mudugudu ufite abahinzi borozi b'icyitegererezo n'abafasha b'amashuri y'abahinzi mu murima bashobora kugusura. Ku bibazo by'ibihingwa baza agronome w'akagari cyangwa w'umurenge; ku buzima bw'amatungo baza veterineri w'umurenge. Menyesha vuba ibyonnyi cyangwa indwara z'amatungo kugira ngo bikumirwe.
